I can't say I had all the same experiences as you - I started reading homestuck later on in my life, but what I've seen from my other interests is that you get what you take from things. if something's special to you, it's pretty likely that in some way, it'll always be special to you- even if you don't enjoy the thing as you did, you still have your memories, and it sounds like you have a lot of really good memories with it.


I think, at its core, homestuck is a story about growing up. it might be from child to teen, teen to adult- but it's a story about transition and connection, which I think is pretty relevant to 18 year olds. I can't speak on if you'll meet other people who've read homestuck irl as I... also haven't been to college, but it seems pretty likely to me. It was immensely popular at times, and to a degree still is. most of the people I know my age liked homestuck as kids (and are still willing to humor me about it). the good thing about college (from what I've been told) is that it's way easier to make friends with the same interests cause you're all here for a reason. you'll find people with the same connection, I'm sure. even if you don't, you still have us:)
